questions.question: What is the core invariant of a curated demonstration dataset?
options: Every accepted example teaches intended behavior, has auditable provenance, and fills a measured need
Every example is generated by the same model
The release contains as many rows as possible
One aggregate quality score is above 80
questions.explanation: A useful release connects every row to an intended behavior, evidence chain, and coverage requirement; raw volume cannot replace those properties.

questions.question: A team needs 12,000 accepted examples and expects a 60% acceptance rate. Approximately how many candidates should it collect?
questions.explanation: Candidate pool equals accepted target divided by acceptance rate: 12,000 / 0.60 = 20,000 candidates.

questions.question: Why should synthetic demonstrations preserve generator and prompt lineage?
options: To trace repeated artifacts, licensing or privacy risks, and correlated model errors
To guarantee every synthetic answer is correct
To remove the need for human review
To make all generated examples independent evidence
questions.explanation: Synthetic generation is scalable but correlated with the generator and prompt. Lineage makes those dependencies and affected records auditable.

questions.question: Why is one average quality score unsafe as a release gate?
options: A strong dimension can hide failed safety, provenance, duplicate, or critical-slice evidence
Quality dimensions cannot be measured
Every release must have identical scores
Only training loss matters
questions.explanation: Independent blocking dimensions prevent an improvement in one area from canceling a privacy incident or a failed critical slice.

questions.question: What is the correct relationship between active curation and random auditing?
options: Use active curation to prioritize valuable reviews and random audits to estimate prevalence
Use active curation for both prioritization and unbiased prevalence estimates
Use random auditing only for synthetic data
Choose either method because they answer the same question
questions.explanation: Active selection intentionally changes which examples are reviewed, while a random sample supports unbiased estimates of overall defect prevalence.

questions.question: Why should semantic clusters be kept together when creating train and evaluation splits?
options: To prevent paraphrases and near-duplicates from leaking across the split
To make the evaluation set larger than training
To ensure every cluster uses one language
To avoid storing record hashes
questions.explanation: Splitting near-duplicates across train and evaluation lets memorized patterns appear as generalization and produces optimistic evidence.

questions.question: A candidate model improves aggregate task quality but the dataset has an unresolved privacy incident. What should happen?
options: Block promotion and investigate the affected records and derived artifacts
Promote because model quality improved
Average privacy with the quality lift
Delete the incident from the dashboard
questions.explanation: Privacy is an independently blocking gate. Aggregate model lift must not override unresolved provenance, privacy, or safety failures.

questions.question: What evidence is still required after dataset-level gates pass?
options: Held-out model behavior, safety, regressions, critical slices, and operational readiness
Only the final row count
Only reviewer agreement
No further evidence because dataset quality proves model quality
questions.explanation: Dataset checks describe the training artifact; only candidate-model evaluation shows how fine-tuning changed the behavior users will receive.
